buildings.name: Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts
Miami-Dade County School Board Administration Building

limitations: The developable surface is Miami-Dade folio 0132310750010, 1 Herald Plaza. Parking west of Herald Plaza is outside this polygon.
The studio brief of 330 by 820 feet and 270,600 square feet is not the drawn boundary. The drawn ring is the parcel. Its bounding width and depth and its ring area are stored on the site record.
Building footprints are Miami-Dade BuildingFootprint2D. A footprint whose centroid is inside the parcel ring is left out, so an older mass is not drawn on the studio site.

Heights marked osm-height are OpenStreetMap height tags converted from meters to international feet. Heights marked county use the county HEIGHT field as feet; the service does not publish a unit, and the populated values in this extract are low-rise numbers, so they are drawn as feet. Heights marked osm-levels are provisional: the story count times 10 feet. Footprints with no height stay flat.

An OpenStreetMap name or height is joined to a county footprint only when that footprint's centroid falls inside the OpenStreetMap building and the county footprint is at least a quarter of its area. Otherwise the OpenStreetMap footprint is added and marked footprintSource osm, including a flat footprint when no height is tagged. A campus outline is not copied onto a small footprint inside it.

Road centerlines follow OpenStreetMap highways clipped to the neighborhood window. Distance uses those centerlines. The default view draws them as thin massing ribbons. The 2024 aerial photograph is an optional verification layer and is off by default.

Where a lidar deck height is stored, the road surface uses that height. A bridge way without a deck return is separated by 0.42 feet so the crossing reads. That separation is drawing order, not a surveyed elevation.
The water surface stays at local zero. No surveyed water elevation was loaded. The west edge is the existing OpenStreetMap coastline. The east edge is a map closure, not a far shore.

Flood and storm surge were not loaded, and the neighborhood ground is not a terrain surface. Bridge decks are lidar heights above the ground at the parcel origin. Building heights still come from the footprint sources, not from lidar.

Causeway, expressway, and ramp decks use 2018 Miami-Dade lidar class-17 returns. The height is above the lidar ground at the parcel origin, not a water elevation. A vertex with no nearby deck return stays on the ground. USGS 3DEP's elevation service here is the ground surface, and the FDOT bridge layer has no deck elevation.

Two offshore county footprints are omitted from the building layer. The finger east of the parcel is OpenStreetMap pier 992943178. The footprint about 950 feet east of North Bayshore Drive sits at the Miami Life Yacht Rentals dock, not on a land parcel.

Where a pavement edge was found on both sides, the drawn width and the drawn center come from Miami-Dade Edge of Pavement. The stored centerline remains the OpenStreetMap line used for distance. Vertices without both edges keep the lane or class width. The pavement layer's feature dates in this neighborhood are 2019 and 2022. Bridge deck heights remain the 2018 lidar samples and are not the I-395 reconstruction.

Footprints without a tagged height use an estimated reference mass. Small footprints are 15 to 40 feet. Compact mid-size footprints are 64 or 110 feet. Long or very large footprints are 36 or 48 feet, so a garage or a complex is not drawn as a tower. The School Board Administration Building uses 7 published floors at 13 feet. Quantum on the Bay uses 130 feet and the Hilton Miami Downtown uses 90 feet, as the shared base of each complex. Their published tower heights are 554 and 536 feet at Quantum and 299 feet at the Hilton, and those heights are not extruded across the whole county footprint. Road vertices without pavement edges on both sides take the width of the nearest measured vertex on the same road. Five roads with no measured edge use a class estimate: 36 feet for a local street and 40 feet for a ramp.

Elevated roads stay one ribbon where a lidar sample is missing: the deck follows the grade between the measured samples. Street, ramp, and highway ends that face each other are joined across the gap. A local street is not joined to an elevated highway, and the two carriageways of a divided road stay apart.

The default ground is a continuous charcoal massing surface. The Miami-Dade County 2024 aerial photograph remains available as an optional verification layer, off by default. It is MapCache MDCImagery layer Image, exported in WGS84 for the neighborhood window and placed on the site tangent plane.

sources.title: 2018 Miami-Dade County lidar, bridge decks
sources.note: NOAA Digital Coast dataset 9271, 2018 Miami-Dade County ITD lidar, COPC tiles 20180605_318152M.copc.laz, 20180605_318152N.copc.laz, 20180605_318451B.copc.laz, 20180605_318451F.copc.laz, 20180605_318151N.copc.laz, 20180605_318451G.copc.laz, 20180605_318452A.copc.laz, 20180605_318151O.copc.laz, 20180605_318451C.copc.laz, 20180605_318451D.copc.laz, 20180605_318151P.copc.laz, 20180605_318452B.copc.laz, 20180605_318452E.copc.laz, 20180605_318452F.copc.laz, 20180605_318451H.copc.laz. Horizontal NAD83(2011) UTM zone 17N meters. Vertical NAVD88 meters, GEOID18, converted to international feet. Bridge decks are ASPRS class 17. A vertex is raised only when at least 8 class-17 returns fall within 18 meters. The drawn height is that median minus the class-2 ground median at the parcel origin (5.1 ft NAVD88). The USGS 3DEP elevation service at this site returns the ground, about 6 ft NAVD88, and does not include the deck. FDOT bridge lines do not publish a deck elevation. Water stays at local zero.

sources.title: Miami-Dade Edge of Pavement
sources.note: MD_Emaps layer 104, queried in WGS84 and projected to the site frame. The county describes the layer as the edge of publicly traveled pavement, including paved shoulders, digitized from 2013 orthophotography inside the urban development boundary and 2012 orthophotography outside it, with a March 2014 planimetric revision. LAST_UPDATED on the features in this neighborhood is 2019 and 2022. FDOT RCI bridge lines were checked and do not publish pavement width or deck elevation, so they were not used to redraw the surface. A vertex is updated only when an edge falls on both sides, 6 to 70 feet away. The drawn center moves onto the midpoint of those edges. The 2018 lidar deck height stays on the OpenStreetMap centerline. Mean offsets from that centerline are a few feet on the local streets and about 8 feet on MacArthur and I-395, so the deck and these edges describe the same corridor. They do not describe the I-395 bridges still under construction.

sources.title: Miami-Dade County 2024 aerial
